Two Kolmogorov Inequalities:. I have gone through the proof of one of them. I should go through the proof of the other in Chung.
See Theorem 8.3.1 on page 249 of A&L or Theorems 5.3.1 and 5.3.2 on pages 116-117 of Chung.
Median of a random variable: Given a random variable \(X\), a value \(c\) which satisfies \[
P(X < c) \leq 1/2 \leq P(X \leq c)
\] is called a median of \(X\). We may denote such a value as \(\operatorname{median}X\).
Levy’s Inequality: Let \(\{X_i\}_{1 \leq i \leq n}\) be independent random variables and define \(S_j \equiv \sum_{i=1}^j X_i\) for \(j=1,\dots,n\). Then \[
P\Big( \max_{1 \leq j \leq n} |S_j - \operatorname{median}(S_j - S_n)| \geq \lambda\Big) \leq 2 P(|S_n| \geq \lambda),
\] where \(\operatorname{median}(S_j - S_n)\) denotes any median of \(S_j - S_n\) for \(j=1,\dots,n\).
If \(\{X_i\}_{1 \leq i \leq n}\) are symmetric around \(0\), that is, if \(X_i^+\) and \(X_i^-\) have the same probability distribution for \(i=1,\dots,n\), then the inequality is reduced to \[
P\Big( \max_{1 \leq j \leq n} |S_j| \geq \lambda\Big) \leq 2 P(|S_n| \geq \lambda).
\] See Theorem 8.3.2 on page 250 of A&L (though there is a small error in the statement of the result).
Lévy’s Theorem: Wow, this proof is pretty intricate, but I made it through.
